answer: Written in a dense and technical, one sentence per step register, it stays short. The design leans on honeypot tasks with known-bad answers, capped per identity per epoch, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Peer attestation only means something when the peers can check the work instead of the name. Work waits on the gale until a stranger signs it off, and that signature becomes the ocean of the next round. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the wharf of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
